# Page 3^page=3
Master Direction - Reserve Bank of India (Unique Identifiers in Financial Markets) Directions, 2026 Identifiers such as the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) and Unique Transaction Identifier (UTI) are key global standards for promoting transparency in the financial markets. The Reserve Bank has mandated the implementation of LEI and UTI for transactions in financial markets regulated by it. The directions for the implementation of these unique identifiers have been issued through various circulars. The directions have now been consolidated and issued in this Master Direction.

# Page 4^page=4
Section –A: Legal Entity Identifier LEI code, a 20-character unique identity code assigned to entities who are parties to a financial transaction, has been conceived of as a key measure to improve the quality and accuracy of financial data systems for better risk management.

# Page 5^page=5
Section –A: Legal Entity Identifier The LEI code shall be applicable to all OTC transactions undertaken by entities other than individuals in the markets for Government securities, money market instruments, foreign exchange instruments and derivatives covered under section 45U of Chapter III-D of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. For users / clients undertaking non-derivative foreign exchange transactions, the LEI code shall be applicable only for transactions involving an amount equivalent to or exceeding USD one million or equivalent thereof in other currencies. LEI ensures that each entity involved in a transaction is clearly and uniquely identified, avoiding confusion due to similar names or structures.

# Page 6^page=6
Framework for implementation of LEI All participants, resident and non-resident, undertaking transactions falling within the scope of these Direction shall obtain an LEI code from a Local Operating Unit (LOU) which is accredited by the Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF). In the case of an LOU in India, the LOU shall be an entity recognised by the Reserve Bank as an issuer of LEI under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. Non-residents that are not legal entities in their country of incorporation (e.g., funds operated by a non-resident parent / management company that are each registered as a Foreign Portfolio Investor) may use the LEI code of the parent / management company. Entities involved in / responsible for executing transactions, reporting or for depository functions in the markets regulated by the Reserve Bank shall capture the LEI code of the transacting participants in their systems. Entities without an LEI code shall not be eligible to undertake transactions in the financial markets regulated by the RBI. Entities shall ensure that their LEI code is considered current under the rules of the global LEI system and has not lapsed.

# Page 7^page=7
Section – B: Unique Transaction Identifier UTI is a unique identifier assigned to an OTC derivative transaction. It has been conceived as one of the key data elements identified globally for reporting OTC derivative transactions with a view to enable policy makers to obtain a comprehensive view of the OTC derivatives market.

# Page 8^page=8
Master Direction - Reserve Bank of India (Unique Identifiers in Financial Markets) Directions, 2026 Section A of the Directions on implementation of Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) shall come into force with immediate effect. Section B of the Directions on implementation of Unique Transaction Identifier (UTI) shall come into effect from January 01, 2027. LEI uniquely identifies the counterparties to a transaction, UTI serves as a single unique reference number for the transaction.

# Page 9^page=9
NOP-INR position of Authorised Dealers As per Master Direction - Risk Management and Inter-Bank Dealings dated July 05, 2016, as amended from time to time, the Reserve Bank may prescribe limits for open positions involving Rupee (NOP-INR) for exchange rate management, depending on market conditions.

# Page 10^page=10
NOP-INR position of Authorised Dealers RBI has now decided that Authorised Dealers shall ensure that their NOP-INR positions in the onshore deliverable market shall be maintained within US$ 100 million at the end of each business day. ADs shall ensure compliance with the above at the earliest but no later than April 10, 2026. Action: The bank sells $360 million in the interbank market. New Calculation: +$450M (Old Position) - $360M (Sale) = +$90 mil.

# Page 11^page=11
Q1. With reference to the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) framework under the Master Direction – RBI (Unique Identifiers in Financial Markets) Directions, 2026, consider the following statements: 1. LEI is a 20-character alphanumeric code assigned to entities participating in financial transactions. 2. LEI is mandatory for all OTC transactions and transactions in Stock exchanges, including Government securities, money market instruments, foreign exchange, and derivatives, when undertaken by entities other than individuals. 3. In case of non-derivative foreign exchange transactions, LEI is required only when the transaction size is USD 10 million or above (or its equivalent). 4. Entities without a valid and current LEI are not permitted to undertake transactions in financial markets regulated by the Reserve Bank of India. Which of the above statements is/are correct? A. 2 and 3 only B. 2, 3 and 4 only C. 1, 2 and 4 only D. 1 and 4 only E. 1, 2, 3 and 4 MCQs for Practice

# Page 12^page=12
Q1. With reference to the Unique Transaction Identifier (UTI) framework under the Master Direction – RBI (Unique Identifiers in Financial Markets) Directions, 2026, consider the following statements: 1. UTI shall be generated for all OTC transactions, including both derivative and non-derivative segments. 2. The UTI consists of a maximum of 52 characters and includes the LEI of the generating entity. 3. In case a transaction is reported to the trade repository without a UTI, the Clearing Corporation of India Limited – Trade Repository (CCIL-TR) may generate the UTI. Which of the above statements is/are correct? A. 1 and 3 only B. 2 only C. 2 and 3 only D. 1, 2 and 3 E. 1 and 2 only MCQs for Practice
